reviews.title: Swinging WAY above its weight class!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1GFGM-bgmL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61vE3YQp0aL._SY256.jpg Solid AIO. No one had a rework written up on it yet so I figured I would be the first.
What I like about this AIO are its performance paired with good looks. It’s sleek, the display is bright and looks crisp, the connectivity is easy, and its performance isn’t sacrificed to give you this.
I’m still running tests on the CPU for thermal limitations and to figure out how long it takes to hit equilibrium, but so far this thing is holding its own against my older arctic 2.
It’s consistently holding my R7 7800X3D at or about the 35c temperature range and under stress it’s not breaking 65c, allowing my CPU to hit boost clock and hold for longer.
What I’m a little skeptical of is the software that comes with it and the radiator thickness. I’m used to having a thicker radiator with more volume in it so I’m a little worried about thermal saturation under heavy pump speeds. Time will tell on this one. At 100.00 I’m willing to take a chance on it and if it lasts me a year or two, I’ll consider it a win for the little guy.
I have another PC running on a v1 peerless assassins, and the cooler hasn’t missed a beat and almost 3 years now, so I do have high hopes, but the jury remains out and I’ll update if something g changes.
My last complaint isn’t so much a complaint as it is more of an old man’s ramblings. The software is fine and serviceable. It does what it says on the box. But Thermalright could do much better if they spend a couple of grand and hire a technical writer to write a manual for the software.
Explaining how the effects layers work, and how you can upload images and use their own stock templates on it would really I think answer a lot of questions people have and soften the user learning curve.
Overall this is a great AIO so far. Time will tell about things like clogging, wear and evaporation rates, but at the price point I’m willing to take that chance and I’m glad I did.
Edit: updated review to reflect my current opinion of the product. After several thermal tests, including an hour long burn in with Cinebench R23 at 100% cpu load, the package temp never broke 70c, and the core temp never broke 60c.
I’m very impressed with this cooler.
reviews.author: Scott Taylor

reviews.title: Just buy it, you won't be sorry.
reviews.comment: This is a great Aio that keeps my CPU at 42 to 55 c under load. The infinity fans fit my theme nicely, I run 11 of them in my build. Very reasonable price for a AIO with the 4.5" screen.
reviews.author: Michael Byers

reviews.title: Excellent cooling and a awesome big screen
reviews.comment:
Pros:
Excellent cooling performance.  Beats out the Liquid Freezer 3 by about 7 degrees under full load with a 7800X3D.  I used Lian Li inf wireless on them which aren't known for their cooling performance, so you could get even better results with the stock fans.
Installation was a breeze.
Display looks great. Bright and vibrant. Good size and easy to read.  Held on by magnets.
Tubing looks more premium than you would expect for the price.
5 year warranty
Price
Cons:
Software is buggy and might not load the background you had selected.  It has lots of cool backgrounds to choose from with animations.
I decided to go with this after seeing reviews of some of their older models and also using their great air coolers. I was trying to decide between this and some more expensive brands like Corsair, Be quiet, and cooler master, but liked the idea of having a screen to play around with.
Even with the software still needing work, I highly recommend this 360 AIO. You could probably check their other coolers for reviews on the fans and the lighting effects.  The are daisy chained and pre installed.

reviews.author: Wally

reviews.title: Incredible!
reviews.comment:
Absolutely blown away!
Who would’ve thought that a well priced and well-made AIO would be on a pedestal. I hate to admit that thermalright has proven me wrong and has put my skepticism at bay if it were not for the subpar software, this would be the end and the beginning of a new era for AIO’s. I am thoroughly pleased. It is quite efficient and has kept my 12900 K under 60°C when running in a cinebench.
It comes in an elegant box and with hose clips to boot, thermal paste and decent hardware. The LCD display is more than I could’ve ever wished for and easy to use. The magnetic base is a godsend and welcomed. The fans sync well with the Asus aura software. Installation was beyond easy. My only gripe is that the film removal on the mirror finish can be a pain, but if you use packaging tape, you can easily remove the film when the included taps fail.
Thermalright has definitely made a presence, but the software needs to improve if they can get the software to be as good as Asus then they will be unstoppable.
